identity.title: Lantern Tide
identity.logline: In a village of drifting lighthouses, an apprentice keeper with a lost year follows the missing oil to a thirteenth light that nobody remembers.
identity.setting: Hearthdrift, twelve lighthouses on linked islets that drift along the warm Lantern Tide, where lamps burn oil pressed from freely given memories.
identity.tone: Cozy, warm and wistful, with soft humour and a little mystery.
content_notes: Fading and loss are gentle and reversible.
Fog and dark water are mildly spooky only.

style_guide.narrator_voice: Warm, second person, present tense. Short sentences, soft humour, lamp and tide imagery.
style_guide.naming_conventions: Plain first names (Hester, Pell, Nim) with surnames from lamp and sea trades (Wick, Tallow, Quay, Reed). Places read like homes or chores (Kettle Quay, Thirteen Buns). Say lost or faded, never amnesia.

lines: Oh, dear. The light flickered again last night, didn't it? Come and sit by the lamp.
Finders keepers, friend! Though I might trade, for something shiny.
Twelve lights. Thirteen berths. Count again. Count properly.
Slow and steady, dear. A good bun is like a good memory, it rises in its own time.
There you are, Spark. You took your time. I kept the lamp warm.

truths.text: There are thirteen berths in the harbour but only twelve lights.
The Keeper of Berth Thirteen was Wren Tallow, and her name is fading from the records.
Remembrance oil is made from freely given memories. Burning it makes the giver fade from others' memories.
Seven years ago the village drifted into the Hush, a fog that smothers lights.
Wren lit the Thirteenth Light with her own memories to guide the village out of the Hush.
The village forgot Wren because her burnt memories erased her from everyone else's.
The missing oil flows down the tide to the Lantern Deep. The Thirteenth Light still burns and is running low.
Wren is alive below the tide, keeping the Drowned Lamp.
The player was Wren's apprentice, Spark, and gave a year of memories to the lamp.
Elder Hobb remembers Wren and kept silent, fearing that speaking her name would put out the lamp.
Burnt memories return when they are remembered together and told aloud at the lamp.
Granny's thirteen-spice bun was Wren's favourite.
The Hush returns in the seventh year, about now.
The banner's thirteenth star is stitched in a hand nobody remembers.
Nim saw an amber glow under the tide.
The Mothlight's flicker is an echo of the Thirteenth Light.
Captain Quay's ship was guided out of the Hush by a small light that sang.
Rook rows to Berth Thirteen at midnight each year to leave a lamp-wick, without knowing why.

clues.text: Thirteen mooring rings, and one empty lamp-stand with nothing to light.
Dorrin counts the lights from Foghorn Rock: twelve, and thirteen berths.
The Founders' banner has thirteen stars, one more than there are lights.
Hester worries that the harbour has a berth too many for its lights.
Dusk Ink brings up a faded ledger line: Berth Thirteen, Keeper W. Tallow.
W.T. is sewn inside an old coat and carved under the cot.
Rook once mended a coat stitched W.T. and cannot say whose it was.
Bramwell mumbles that oil is pressed from memories freely given, and that givers fade.
The founders' recipe book describes oil made from given memories.
A copied page of the founders' recipe says burning the oil fades the giver.
A plaque on the cistern thanks every giver of a memory.
Dorrin's barometer lore: the village drifted into the Hush seven years ago.
The Pilchard's scorched log records the Hush seven years ago.
Quay remembers the Hush swallowing his ship's lamp seven years ago.
The Oil Press tally shows the oil ran cold seven years ago.
Hester says the Mothlight went dark seven years ago, in the Hush.
Quay tells of a small light that sang and led his ship out of the fog.
The Bell Tower ledger shows the thirteenth bell rung once that night.
Rook heard a small light that sang, the night of the Hush.
A copy of the Bell Tower ledger page shows the lamp lit that night.
Tamsin says names fade in the order the lamps were lit.
Granny bakes thirteen buns and cannot say why her notes fade.
The Mothlight flickers as if answering a name nobody can recall.
The Oil Press tally ledger shows the loss following the tide.
Amber threads of oil drift downward through the kelp.
Nim says the tide runs warm and amber down the steps.
Amber threads flow in at the gallery windows towards a distant light.
Nim says the girl in the water waves back.
Through the brass spyglass, a glow shows below the tide.
A warm glow with a small figure sitting beside it.
Wren greets the player and says she has kept the lamp warm.
The apprentice cot and scarf bear the player's own handwriting.
Lumi chimes the word Spark and circles the player.
An apprentice hook at the Mothlight Base, with the player's half-sewn tag matching its thread.
Wren calls the player Spark and asks about the lost year.
Rook squints at the player and says aye, you were Spark.
In Hobb's study sits a locket engraved with a wren.
Hobb's unsent letters to Wren, tied with string, lie in a cellar box.
Hobb quietly admits he remembers his granddaughter.
The founders' chorus rite page says burnt memories return when told aloud together.
The Empty Flask and a remembered bun make the cistern hum.
Wren explains that the village must tell its memories of her together.
Granny says the thirteen-spice bun was a young keeper's favourite.
Pell admits the brass spyglass belonged to the thirteenth keeper.
Dorrin's mended barometer says the Hush returns in seven years, which is now.
Yarrow notices the thirteenth star is in a hand she does not know.
Nim points at the tidepool, where an amber glow shimmers under the water.
Hester says the Mothlight flickers like an echo of another lamp.
Quay tells it true: a small light that sang led his ship out of the Hush.
Rook admits he rows to Berth Thirteen each year with a lamp-wick.
The player's half-sewn name tag has only a few stitched letters.
Villagers whisper that Pell takes oil from the press.
Tamsin suspects Bramwell of taking oil from the press.
Hobb warns the player not to go asking about the harbour.
Hobb's study door is locked and his lamp burns late.
A pale ghost light drifts in the fog at the edge of the Hush.
Wet oars and a small boat tied up after midnight on Tallow Row.
Sailors say a bad-luck lamp sits in the wreck of the Pilchard.

twists.description: You were her apprentice. The half-sewn name tag and Rook's recognition point to the player's past as Spark.
The suspected thief is a lamp. The missing oil flows down the tide to the Thirteenth Light.
The villain remembers. Hobb was protecting the lamp, not hiding a crime.

red_herrings.description: Pell is suspected of stealing oil from the press. In the Medium length Tamsin suspects Bramwell instead.
red_herrings.resolution: Pell only collects lost things, and the oil is not stolen: the lamp in the Deep draws it.

red_herrings.description: A ghost light drifts in the Whisper Fog Edge.
red_herrings.resolution: The pale lights are only glow-moths.

red_herrings.description: Rook rows out at midnight and nobody knows why.
red_herrings.resolution: He leaves a lamp-wick at Berth Thirteen each year, without knowing why.

red_herrings.description: Sailors say the Wreck of the Pilchard holds a bad-luck lamp.
red_herrings.resolution: It holds only old signalling mirrors.
It holds only a locket and letters to Wren.

endings.scene_outline: The village gathers at Berth Thirteen and each tells Wren's name and a memory. The lamp is relit above the tide, Wren returns, and the player regains their lost year. In the Short length the choice is saying her name at the berth.
endings.epilogue_notes: Vary the epilogue with the goals the player resolved. Shared conditions are the core truths common to every length.

endings.scene_outline: Wren stays as the lamp's keeper. The village remembers her and the Thirteenth Light shines beside the others. The player visits often.
endings.epilogue_notes: Hobb and Wren share the harbour at dusk. The player keeps their year.

endings.scene_outline: The lamp holds one more year and the Hush passes. The village stays cosy but forgetful, and the player keeps one lantern burning for her.
endings.tone: Gentle and wistful. A fallback ending.
endings.epilogue_notes: Wren waves from the water. The player promises to come back.

endings.scene_outline: Every villager brings a lantern, the banner flies with thirteen stars, and the Hush never comes back.
endings.tone: Triumphant and joyful. A secret bonus ending.
endings.epilogue_notes: Mention each resolved subplot by name.
